thread:
anya_support: Customer reported a surge of 429s and timeouts on their Dedicated pool this morning. They say it started after a batch job with very long contexts. Attaching brief logs and error headers.
anya_support: Logs snippet:
```
2026-03-12T09:02:13Z ERROR tenant=acct-298 call_id=abc123 gen=12 kvcache.evict "eviction_count=1420" "fragmentation=0.72"
2026-03-12T09:02:15Z WARN  tenant=acct-298 runtime throttle "429=seq_kv_pressure"
2026-03-12T09:02:18Z ERROR tenant=acct-298 request_id=xyz789 longctx fail "alloc_failed"
```

anya_support: Customer repro steps they gave:
- send 20 concurrent requests with context ~120k tokens
- sustained 3 min burst
- many requests see streaming stall or 429s

dave_infra: Can you paste the cluster id + node list? I want to check slab allocation and if autoscaler did anything around 09:02. Also which Dedicated tier (ded-std/ded-pro)?
anya_support: Cluster: ded-nyc-3, nodes: gpu-3a,gpu-3b,gpu-3c. Tier: ded-pro.

mike_ops: Quick metric checks: PromQL to see KV slab churn / eviction rate:
```promql
sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total{cluster=\"ded-nyc-3\"}[1m])) by (tenant)
/
sum(kv_cache_entries{cluster=\"ded-nyc-3\"}) by (tenant)
```
If fragmentation > 0.6 and spike in evictions coincides with burst, it's likely long contexts are causing large KV growth -> heap scatter -> fragmentation.

kyle_se: Repro note from infra: long-context workloads with lots of distinct prefixes blow up number of KV entries (each token sequence/state pinned). For quick repro we ran this locally: 
```bash
for i in {1..20}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/requests 
    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" 
    -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-long-1\",\"input\":\"'$(yes \"word\" | head -n 120000 | tr -d '\\n')'\"}' &
done; wait
```
This produced similar eviction waves in our staging dedicated pool.
autoscaler-bot: [09:03:02] autoscaler event: cluster=ded-nyc-3 scale_up suggested=1 reason=\"sustained_queue\"

autoscaler-bot: [09:04:40] autoscaler event: cluster=ded-nyc-3 scale_up executed=0 reason=\"scale_blocked_by_quota\"

sam_engineer: Short term mitigation options:
- Pin tenant to isolated pool (create temp pool and move tenant)
- Reduce per-tenant kv_max_entries or set tenant_kv_cap so single tenant can't fragment others
- Temporarily increase slab_chunk_size and restart runtime on nodes (downtime)
- Add request-level guard: reject requests > 40k tokens with 413 to avoid full blast

mike_ops: Also check GC/alloc logs on nodes: `/var/log/redwood/runtime_alloc.log` - look for \"alloc_lock_stall\" and per-slab free list sizes. If free list gets many small fragments, fragmentation metric climbs.
dave_infra: I see the quota blocking autoscale — ops already on it. For now I moved acct-298 to a prewarmed spare node (noisy-tenant isolation) and bumped tenant_kv_cap to 15% of node. That dropped eviction rate ~70% in 2 minutes.

anya_support: Customer update: moved them to isolated node and they report reduced 429s. They're asking for root cause and permanent fix.

sam_engineer: Root cause summary (short): long-context concurrent requests created a very high cardinality of KV keys, causing aggressive eviction and memory fragmentation. Fragmentation prevented the runtime from reusing slabs efficiently -> alloc failures -> throttling. Permanent fixes: enforce per-request limits, per-tenant KV caps, smarter slab defragmenter, and autoscaler quota safety to allow emergency scale.

anya_support: Filed support ticket INC-2026-298 and flagged as Sev-3. Assigning to @dave_infra and @sam_engineer for follow-up with product for quota policy change.
dave_infra: Acknowledge. I'll coordinate with finance + capacity to relax scale blocking windows for ded-pro short emergencies.

mike_ops: Follow-up: I'll add a dashboard panel for \"perm_kv_cardinality\"/tenant and alert when it crosses 50k distinct keys in 1m. Also adding a small evict hysteresis so bursts don't produce full cascade.

anya_support: Thanks everyone :thumbsup: I'll send the customer a summary and ETA for the permanent changes.
